description: Table — the density centerpiece. Rows and cells are DOM elements, not classable parts; the invariant holds PER CELL (padding = inset − halfLeading), so row heights emerge (24/36/44) and switching density shows MORE ROWS in the same viewport — never a narrower table. That asymmetry is the point: the horizontal/vertical spacing split is the prepared seam.
notes: Row hover rides the neutral ghost ladder; the selected row binds the accent ghost-selected rung — same mechanism as menu items, because a table row IS a transparent-resting interactive surface. Column widths are content's business (Figma: column-major grid, columns hug). Sorting, virtualization and cell renderers are application concerns. v0.2.0 (2026-09-06, Victor, from the Storefront's props tables): the COMPRESSED size, for big data tables. sm cells in an sm-squished inset; the invariant holds per cell, so rows land 20/24/36 across densities (8+8+8 at comfortable), still never authored. The size is a channel-variable override in CSS (data-size='compressed' repoints the five size variables). Figma disposition: LOWERED for now; the canvas table ships the Default size only, until the table builder learns per-variant cell bindings (queued in SCOPE). v0.3.0 (2026-09-06, Victor, from Google Sheets' wrapped cells measured at ~1.35): CELL TEXT IS READ, NOT SCANNED — both sizes move to the default leading (md 14/20, compressed sm 12/16) and the vertical padding absorbs the larger half-leading, so every row height stays exactly where it was (24/36/44 and 20/24/36): the leading variant changes the padding, never the height — the invariant's own promise, applied to prose in cells. Header cells ride the same leading (an accepted trade: headers are scanned labels, but they are single-line, so the shared leading is invisible and keeps ONE padding pairing per size on both surfaces).

props.name: size
props.description: Row density WITHIN a density mode: default (md cells, sm-squared inset) for reading tables, compressed (sm cells, sm-squished inset) for big data tables. Heights stay emergent: 24/36/44 default, 20/24/36 compressed.
